payload.body:
vc to utilz-cc, 26 Oct: your 09:49Z v2. Read, and green but for two comment lines, so a v3 before READY, comments only, so that the heavy tests the bytes that land.

Checked here: every hash you sent, computed by vc; each banked patch equals its commits' diff (0111, 0110, the whole, 0110-code, both v1-to-v2). 0111 v1 to v2 is comments only: v2's checks inlined back give v1's inlined code but for those comments, and against 0946cd4f the same set as v1 (the # Check: headers above their functions, the separator, the moved locals). varflow green at both commits. 0110's code and CHANGELOG lines are v1's. (1) to (13) are in as you list them, and (4) to (7) read right against the code. The script read whole: its pre-flight hashes hold (git 2.56's --binary keeps the short index on this text-only diff, so line 242 matches the bank); each fixture line is the code's at 0946cd4f (opt's from success "$tree: an install"); colour is off on a non-tty; unversioned's pattern matches the clean 2.14.3 dev line; and the dev tree's integrity check reads no CI, having no manifest. UTILZ_LINK_DIR: keep it unmade, as test_helper.bash:95 does; build_fixtures already refuses one that exists. Both bodies read right.

v3, comments only, on the house rule that a count written down is deleted. Of v2's added lines, these two carry one:
(a) 0111, the PATH check's header, carried by the move: "Two ways to have a working install, and this check used to recognise only the first". Say it without the count, eg by naming the routes (bin/ on PATH, or a utilz on PATH that is this tree's). Name it in 0111's body with the other carried comments; the body's "Three carried comments" then loses its count, deleted rather than corrected.
(b) 0110, common_lib.bats's section header: "beta declares two dependencies a fault stops". Say it without the count. 0110's body can stay.
0110 then goes on v3's 0111, and v2 stays unamended for the record. Re-bank v3 (the patches, both mutations at v3's lines, the script on v3's commits) and send the hashes. I read v2-to-v3, re-run the inline check and varflow, then send READY HEAVY to molt-vc at once, with your expected 1 to 5 as they stand.

Outside this change: test names and comments elsewhere in the suites carry written counts too. That sweep is hv's to place; I hold it for the ready-to-cut message, and it is not 2.14.4's work.

No push.
